summary: Modern databases and data platforms increasingly embed AI/ML directly into the data layer, allowing SQL-based model inference, LLM access, and vector similarity search without moving data to separate systems. Capabilities range from built-in LLM functions (Snowflake Cortex, BigQuery ML) to native vector indexes (MongoDB Atlas, Databricks Vector Search) and in-database model hosting via cloud AI services. This trend reflects a broader market shift, with vector-based retrieval for GenAI projected to grow rapidly through 2034 as enterprises adopt RAG and agentic architectures.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI (LLM functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless SQL and Python functions for LLM tasks (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, EXTRACT_ANSWER), embedding generation, and fine-tuning. Cortex Search offers a managed hybrid retrieval service for RAG, and Cortex Analyst enables natural-language querying of structured data. Snowflake Postgres also exposes Cortex functions directly from Postgres.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in VECTOR data type with VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY / VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE functions and managed Cortex Search service. Snowflake Postgres adds vector capabilities alongside Cortex integration.
databases.llm_integration: Native hosted LLMs (Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic, and others) accessible via SQL/Python; no external API keys required.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based pricing billed in Snowflake credits by tokens processed or compute used; Cortex Search and serverless functions billed per usage. No separate licensing.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI and Gemini integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets users create and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, forecasting, boosted trees, DNNs) using SQL. Through remote models it connects to Vertex AI and Gemini for text generation, embeddings, translation, and multimodal AI directly from SQL via ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native vector search via the VECTOR_SEARCH function and CREATE VECTOR INDEX (IVF/TreeAH) on ARRAY columns storing embeddings.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Vertex AI foundation models including Gemini; also supports Hugging Face and partner models through remote model endpoints.
databases.pricing_notes: Billed via BigQuery compute (on-demand per TB scanned or capacity slots) plus Vertex AI API charges for generative/embedding calls. Some built-in ML models train within BigQuery pricing.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector extension plus pgai / pgvectorscale for in-database AI
databases.description: pgvector adds vector storage and similarity search to PostgreSQL. The pgai extension (Timescale) brings embedding creation and LLM calls (OpenAI, Ollama, Anthropic, etc.) into SQL, while pgvectorscale improves indexing scalability. Together they enable RAG pipelines inside open-source Postgres.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native in the sense of a widely adopted first-party-style extension (pgvector) with HNSW and IVFFlat indexes; vector search is not part of core Postgres but is enabled via the pgvector extension, which is the de facto standard.
databases.llm_integration: Via pgai, which calls external LLM/embedding providers (OpenAI, Cohere, Anthropic, Ollama, Hugging Face) from SQL functions; no built-in hosted models.
databases.pricing_notes: Open source and free; costs depend on the hosting platform (self-managed, RDS, Cloud SQL, Timescale) plus any external LLM API fees.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning (SageMaker, Bedrock, and Comprehend integration)
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you invoke ML models from SQL queries, passing row data to Amazon SageMaker endpoints, Amazon Comprehend for NLP, and Amazon Bedrock foundation models for generative AI and embeddings, with results returned inline in the query.
databases.vector_search_notes: Aurora PostgreSQL supports vector search only through the pgvector extension, not as a native Aurora ML feature; Aurora MySQL lacks native vector search. Therefore native built-in vector search is not provided by Aurora ML itself.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock models (e.g., Anthropic Claude, Titan) and SageMaker-hosted models via SQL functions like aws_bedrock.invoke_model.
databases.pricing_notes: No extra charge for the Aurora ML feature itself; you pay standard Aurora costs plus the underlying SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend usage charges.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML (SageMaker Autopilot, Bedrock, and bring-your-own-model)
databases.description: Redshift ML enables creating, training, and deploying ML models using the CREATE MODEL SQL command, backed by Amazon SageMaker Autopilot. It supports in-database inference, remote inference to SageMaker endpoints, and generative AI through Amazon Bedrock LLM integration.
databases.vector_search_notes: Redshift does not provide a native vector index/search service; similarity can be computed manually on numeric arrays but there is no built-in ANN vector search. Vector workloads are typically offloaded to OpenSearch or pgvector elsewhere.
databases.llm_integration: Generative AI via Amazon Bedrock large language models invoked from SQL, plus custom models hosted in SageMaker.
databases.pricing_notes: No additional charge for Redshift ML commands beyond Redshift compute; training and inference incur SageMaker and Bedrock usage costs.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training, serving, agents) and Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Mosaic AI provides end-to-end GenAI tooling: foundation model APIs, fine-tuning, model serving, agent frameworks, and evaluation, all governed by Unity Catalog. Databricks Vector Search offers a managed, auto-syncing vector index built on Delta tables for RAG applications.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in managed Vector Search service with automatic embedding and syncing from Delta tables; supports both self-managed and Databricks-computed embeddings.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Foundation Model APIs host and serve open and proprietary LLMs (Llama, DBRX, Mistral, plus external models like OpenAI/Anthropic via external endpoints).
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs) for compute, model serving, and Vector Search endpoints; foundation model usage billed per token or per endpoint.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search and Atlas AI integrations
databases.description: Atlas Vector Search stores embeddings alongside operational documents and performs approximate nearest-neighbor search using HNSW indexes, enabling RAG and semantic search without a separate vector database. It integrates with popular AI frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex) and supports hybrid and filtered vector queries.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in vector search via the $vectorSearch aggregation stage and a dedicated vectorSearch index type within Atlas.
databases.llm_integration: No native hosted LLMs; integrates with external providers (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, Hugging Face) and orchestration frameworks for embedding generation and generation.
databases.pricing_notes: Included within Atlas cluster pricing; dedicated Search Nodes can be provisioned for scaling, billed by instance size. External embedding/LLM API costs are separate.
